plain_english: Everything has two handles — one that lets you carry it, and one that doesn't. If your brother treats you unfairly, don't grab onto his unfairness. That handle won't work. Instead, grab onto the fact that he's your brother and you grew up together. That's the handle that will let you carry this burden.
original_excerpt: Everything has two handles: one by which it may be borne, another by which it cannot. If your brother acts unjustly, do not lay hold on the affair by the handle of his injustice, for by that it cannot be borne, but rather by the opposite—that he is your brother, that he was brought up with you; and thus you will lay hold on it as it is to be borne.
